transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-11
Start: 16:00 UTC (09:00 PDT)
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Omar (Redwood CSM); Marta (StratusHealth CTO), Ethan (Platform), Lisa (InfoSec), Devon (ML)

Summary: quick scoping for a pilot to decide deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Focus on success criteria (latency, throughput, SLOs), realistic benchmark plan, data residency/compliance constraints, and timeline for a 2-4 week POC.

Topics: Success criteria, traffic profile, model sizing, hardware needs, networking (VPC), SOC2/KMS, pilot acceptance criteria, pricing + contract triggers.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll go 50 minutes or so, try to get through success criteria and a bench plan. Um Priya will run through the technical ask.
[00:22] Priya: Hi all, quick agenda, 1) what you're trying to validate in the pilot, 2) traffic and model details, 3) benchmark matrix (latency/throughput/quality), 4) decision criteria for hosting.
[00:38] Marta: Thanks, our key driver is latency for clinical chat assist, plus strict PHI rules — so security is huge. We want to understand if Hosted can meet p95 latency and policies, or we need Dedicated or Private.
[00:55] Lisa: Right, anything with PHI likely forces data residency and encryption controls; we need KMS/HSM and audit logs. Also SSO/SAML for RBAC.
[01:10] Ethan: On traffic, current chat baseline is around 5 rps steady with 50 concurrent sessions peak in a clinic hour; expected pilot load is 20 rps bursty. Most requests are short context (~512 tokens) but we have some longer case notes up to 2k tokens.
[01:35] Priya: Good — that informs sequence length and KV cache expectations. For model, are you planning to run an open LLM or a hosted model?
[01:45] Devon: We prefer an open model to avoid vendor lock. We'll test a 7B and a 13B quantized variant. Quality needs to be within our eval thresholds — measured by rouge-like metrics and a human score sample.
[02:05] Jordan: To surface differences: Hosted = fastest to start, pay-per-use, Redwood manages everything; Dedicated = reserved GPU pools in our infra with isolation and predictable throughput; Private = customer-controlled VPC/on-prem with our control plane optionally air-gapped.
[02:30] Marta: The big question is whether Hosted can pass our InfoSec bar. Lisa, are you comfortable with an initial hosted pilot if we can get SOC2 and a specific data retention SLA?
[02:43] Lisa: Maybe. We need proof of encryption at rest with customer-managed keys, detailed audit logs, and minimum retention controls. If those are present, a short sandbox hosted pilot could be OK, but production likely needs Private or Dedicated depending on SLA.
[03:05] Priya: Noted. For benchmarks — suggest we run three scenarios: 1) latency SLA test (p50/p95 tail with 512 tokens), 2) throughput stress (sustained 20-50 rps), 3) mixed workload with long tails (up to 2k tokens). We'll capture token-level cost and failure modes.
[03:30] Ethan: For throughput, we also want to test cold-start behavior and KV cache hit rates — many of our sessions re-use earlier context. How does Redwood expose cache controls?
[03:45] Priya: There are KV cache knobs and prefix caching semantics; in Hosted we manage cache and can give stats, in Dedicated/Private customers can tune cache size. We'll include cache-enabled and cache-disabled runs in the plan.
[04:05] Jordan: Also decision criteria: latency thresholds, consistent throughput, data control (KMS, VPC), cost per 1M tokens, and operational responsibility. For the pilot acceptance, propose: p95 < 400ms for 512-token doc generation, < 750ms for 2k tokens? - open to discussion.
[04:30] Marta: Those numbers seem optimistic; our clinical UX target is p95 < 300ms for quick assistant prompts. If not possible server-side, we might need heavier client-side caching.
[04:45] Priya: Understood. We can run baseline numbers to see feasible p95. For open models quantized on A100 or T4 equivalents, p95 for 512 tokens is typically in the 200-500ms range depending on packing and batch. There will be variance.
[05:10] Lisa: Also compliance: data residency — we must keep all PHI within US regions. Any cross-region fallback must be disabled.
[05:22] Jordan: We can lock region and disable cross-region fallback for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be pinned to US only if account setup supports it; we'll confirm.
[05:35] Ethan: On networking, if we do Dedicated we need peering and strict egress rules; Private/on-prem will require an install plan. What's the rough timeline to get Private up for a pilot?
[05:50] Priya: Private on-prem is longer — typically 6-8 weeks for install, validation, and KMS integration. Dedicated can be provisioned 1-2 weeks after contract; Hosted is immediate. For a 2-4 week pilot we may need Hosted or Dedicated.
[06:10] Devon: From ML side, we want to validate both quality and latency. We'll supply evaluation prompts and holdouts. What's the benchmark structure?
[06:20] Priya: We'll run: 50 synthetic prompts for quality scoring, then 3 load patterns for perf. We'll capture p50/p95, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also track error rates and tail latencies.
[06:45] Jordan: Pricing triggers: if pilot meets acceptance and load increases beyond an agreed threshold, we shift to Dedicated reservation with X-month commit. We should include cost modeling in the deliverables.
[07:00] Marta: One more Org constraint: procurement needs an SOW and a security questionnaire answered. We prefer a short SOW for the pilot with clear success criteria and exit criteria.
[07:15] Jordan: We'll produce a pilot SOW template.
[07:22] Priya: Quick question to Ethan — what does your current infra look like? Are you on single cloud or multi-cloud?
[07:30] Ethan: Primary in AWS (us-east-1), some GCP experiments. Network is VPC with strict private subnets for PHI. We can do VPC peering for Dedicated. Private would need an install on an approved subnet.
[07:48] Priya: Good. For the pilot we need a small test VPC for connectivity tests if Dedicated; or a hosted sandbox account with US-only region. We'll add explicit network tests to the bench plan.
[08:05] Lisa: Also, do you offer HSM integration for KMS? Our policy mandates customer-managed keys for certain datasets.
[08:15] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated support customer KMS; Hosted can integrate with customer-managed keys in some enterprise accounts — we'll confirm with Security.
[08:30] Devon: For model variants, we'll test 7B quantized and 13B quantized. Can Redwood run both on the same cluster or do we need separate instance types?
[08:45] Priya: We can run mixed model catalogs but for performance isolation Dedicated allows pinning workloads to different GPU types. For Hosted we'll schedule variants on compatible hardware, but noisy neighbor can affect p95. We'll capture that in the bench.
[09:05] Ethan: Ok. For acceptance criteria, let's propose concrete numbers: 1) p95 < 350ms for 512 tokens, 2) sustained throughput 20 rps with <2% error rate, 3) audit logs recorded and available within 24 hours, 4) region locked to us-east-1. Thoughts?
[09:28] Lisa: Acceptable if audit and KMS controls are validated.
[09:33] Jordan: We'll aim to meet those. If Hosted can't meet audit/KMS, Dedicated is likely the path. We'll run initial hosted sandbox to measure raw performance while parallelly working contract for Dedicated.
[09:50] Priya: I'll draft a benchmark matrix and a runbook. Proposed timeline: this week Ethan shares traffic samples + infra; Redwood shares SOC2 and network checklist; Priya delivers benchmark plan by 2025-06-18; pilot kickoff target 2025-06-23 for a 2-week experimental window.
[10:15] Marta: That timeline works for us if procurement can quick-turn the SOW.
[10:25] Jordan: Noted. Any blockers?
[10:30] Lisa: Our blocker is KMS and audit proof for Hosted; if Redwood can demonstrate those we might accept Hosted for pilot. Otherwise Dedicated.
[10:40] Priya: For benchmarking specifics — we'll run these bucketed tests: small (512 tokens) with concurrency ramps, medium (1024 tokens), and long (2k tokens). We'll record GPU metrics every 10s and token emit rates.
[10:55] Devon: We'll include human eval batch for quality. We'll give a 200-sample holdout for human scoring.
[11:05] Jordan: Great. I'll follow up with pricing examples and SOW template. Priya will send bench plan. Ethan will provide traffic samples. Lisa to share compliance checklist.
[11:20] Marta: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the clarity.
[11:25] Jordan: End recap: deliverables and owners as action items, tentative pilot start 2025-06-23, decision to go Dedicated if Hosted cannot meet KMS/audit needs.
[11:40] Priya: I'll add KV cache and cold-start scenarios to the bench matrix.
[11:50] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had a few mis-heards (KV cache -> K V cash, some acronyms mangled), cleaned lightly but preserved speaker interruptions and filler.

Acceptance criteria (as captured):
- Performance: p95 < 350ms for 512-token common prompts; sustain 20 rps with <2% error rate
- Security: Customer-managed KMS or equivalent, audit logs, region lock to us-east-1
- Operational: Bench results within 3 business days of test completion, SOW signed for Dedicated if scaling needed
